parsed.rationale: The structural evidence shows a Jaccard similarity of null and shared_field_count of 0, meaning the two protocols share no members whatsoever. `HLSAVPlayerProtocol` (line 20, HLSPlayer module) exposes HLS/AVPlayer-specific members such as `seekableTimeRanges:[NSValue]`, `seek:(to time: CMTime) async -> Bool`, and `rate:Float`, while `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` (line 34, MP3Streamer module) exposes audio-engine-specific members such as `installRenderTap:()`, `scheduleBuffer:(_ buffer: AVAudioPCMBuffer)`, `eventStream:AsyncStream<AudioPlayerEvent>`, and `volume:Float`. The only surface-level overlap is the presence of a `pause:()` and `play:()` verb in both, but `play:()` on `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` is `throws` while on `HLSAVPlayerProtocol` it is not, making even those two members non-identical in contract. Introducing a shared parent protocol would force an artificial abstraction across two fundamentally different playback subsystems (HLS streaming vs. PCM audio engine), creating a leaky abstraction with no real shared behaviour to factor out.
